back: Push factors drive people away from the origin (unemployment, drought, conflict); pull factors attract them to the destination (jobs, services, safety).
Money sent home by migrants to their families.
Cost, distance, immigration laws, language, lack of information and family ties.

front: Positive impacts on a source area?
back: Remittances, less pressure on jobs and land, skills and savings brought back by returning migrants.

front: Negative impacts on a source area?
back: Loss of young and skilled people (brain drain), older age structure, labour shortages and family separation.
Gains: workers, taxes, diversity. Costs: pressure on housing and services, job competition, social tension.

front: Which people gain least from migration?
back: Migrants who work in poor conditions and face discrimination or exploitation.

front: Qatar as an example of international migration?
back: Migrants are roughly 85 to 90% of residents; kafala system criticised; reforms in 2020 (changing jobs, leaving) and a minimum wage in 2021.

front: Effect of emigration on the dependency ratio?
back: Working-age emigrants lower the denominator, so the dependency ratio rises.
